title: Medical Baseline Allowance Quantities by Protection — Medical and Life-Support Protections
content:
The medical baseline allowance quantities of Medical and Life-Support Protections are stated per qualifying device per day, by the season of the bill, with an additional winter quantity for agreements whose space heating is electric, a limit on the devices counted and a largest allowance per bill.

## Allowance quantities

| Protection | Summer-season bills (kWh per device per day) | Winter-season bills (kWh per device per day) | Electric heat addition on winter-season bills (kWh per day) | Most qualifying devices counted | Largest allowance on one bill (kWh) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 (no allowance) |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | 12 | 12 | 0 | 2 | 750 |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | 16.5 | 13 | 8 | 1 | 850 |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | 24 | 20 | 8 | 2 | 1200 |
| Life-Support Registration | 16.5 | 16.5 | 0 | 2 | 1000 |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | 24 | 24 | 0 | 3 | 1500 |

The electric heat addition is a quantity per day, not per device, and applies only on winter-season bills where the service agreement's space heating is electric.

## What the allowance does, how it is computed and how it is rounded

| Protection | What the allowance changes on the bill | Basis for a billing period | Rounding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medical Emergency Certificate | no allowance | not applicable | not applicable |
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | raises the inclining-block threshold of Schedule RS bills; no allowance value on schedules without an inclining block | per-day allowance times qualifying devices times days in the billing period | rounded to the nearest whole kWh |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | raises the inclining-block threshold of Schedule RS bills; no allowance value on schedules without an inclining block | per-day allowance times qualifying devices times days in the billing period, plus the electric heat bonus per day on winter bills | rounded to the nearest whole kWh |
| Combined Medical Baseline Allowance | raises the inclining-block threshold of Schedule RS bills; no allowance value on schedules without an inclining block | per-day allowance times qualifying devices times days in the billing period, plus the electric heat bonus per day on winter bills | rounded to the nearest whole kWh |
| Life-Support Registration | raises the inclining-block threshold of Schedule RS bills; no allowance value on schedules without an inclining block | per-day allowance times qualifying devices times days in the billing period | rounded to the nearest whole kWh |
| Critical Care Life-Support Registration | raises the inclining-block threshold of Schedule RS bills; no allowance value on schedules without an inclining block | per-day allowance times qualifying devices times days in the billing period | rounded to the nearest whole kWh |

## Schedule notes

- A largest-allowance figure of 0 means no allowance: the Medical Emergency Certificate carries none.
- The Standard Medical Baseline Allowance, the Life-Support Registration and the Critical Care Life-Support Registration carry the same quantity in both seasons; the Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance and the Combined Medical Baseline Allowance carry a higher summer quantity and the winter electric heat addition.
- The allowance raises the inclining-block threshold of Schedule RS bills. Schedules without an inclining block carry no allowance value.

### Hypothetical comparison (30-day billing period, devices at the counted maximum)

| Protection | Summer bill | Winter bill, space heating electric |
|---|---|---|
| Standard Medical Baseline Allowance | 12 times 2 times 30, which is 720 kWh | 12 times 2 times 30, which is 720 kWh |
| Heating and Cooling Medical Baseline Allowance | 16.5 times 1 times 30, which is 495 kWh | 13 times 1 times 30 plus 8 times 30, which is 630 kWh |

Both comparison figures stay below the largest allowance of their protection (750 and 850 kWh respectively).
